display.purpose: Page and hero headlines; Hubot Sans 800 with negative tracking.

body.purpose: Reading text; Inter 400 at ~720px column width.

annotation.purpose: Caveat hand marks only; never UI, labels, or body.

mono.purpose: System markers, status chips, and code blocks; Menlo.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Default hover lift for cards and buttons; the only step most surfaces ever use.

motion.name: marquee-trace
motion.purpose: One-time Signal Orange comet that traces a card perimeter on scroll-into-view, staggered across a grid, then settles to the hairline.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main call-to-action; Signal Orange, used for 'Get in touch' and primary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-weight: 800; font-size: 14px; background: var(--color-primary); color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 10px; height: 48px; padding: 0 32px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-primary-dark); color: var(--color-primary-light); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-primary); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Lower-emphasis action; paper with an ink border that inverts on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-weight: 800; font-size: 14px; background: #fff; color: var(--color-neutral-dark); border: 1px solid var(--color-neutral-dark); border-radius: 10px; height: 48px; padding: 0 32px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; cursor: pointer; transition: all 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--color-neutral-dark); color: #fff; transform: translateY(-1px); }

components.name: Section Badge
components.description: Uppercase eyebrow pill with an icon; anchors the top of most sections.
components.html: About Me
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-primary-light); border: 1.5px solid var(--color-primary); border-radius: 9999px; padding: 8px 24px; } .ds-badge svg { width: 24px; height: 24px; color: var(--color-primary); } .ds-badge__label { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-weight: 700; font-size: 14px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--color-primary); }

components.name: Selection-Frame Card
components.description: Flat card defined by a hairline; on hover the border warms to a 45% Signal Orange tint (the comet-trace runs once on scroll-into-view in-app).
components.html:
UX & Design Practice

Accessibility-first design, systems thinking, and the governance that keeps them honest.
components.css: .ds-card { position: relative; background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(27,27,27,0.1); border-radius: 12px; padding: 32px; transition: border-color 250ms ease-in-out, box-shadow 250ms ease-in-out; } .ds-card:hover { border-color: rgba(240,61,1,0.45); box-shadow: 0 2px 4px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.15); } .ds-card__title { font-family: var(--font-heading); font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; color: var(--color-neutral-dark); margin: 0 0 16px; } .ds-card__body { font-family: var(--font-body); font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--color-neutral-standard); margin: 0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Paper field with a hairline border that shifts to Signal Orange on focus (no glow).
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: var(--font-body); font-size: 16px; color: var(--color-neutral-dark); background: #fff; border: 1px solid rgba(27,27,27,0.1); border-radius: 8px; padding: 8px 12px; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--color-primary); }

components.name: Section Rule
components.description: Signature divider: a numbered marker on a hairline, bookended by 5px square selection handles (the Figma bounding-box motif).
components.html: 04
components.css: .ds-rule { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; width: 100%; } .ds-rule__line { flex: 1; height: 1px; background: var(--color-neutral-light); } .ds-rule__handle { flex-shrink: 0; width: 5px; height: 5px; background: var(--color-secondary); } .ds-rule__num { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-neutral-muted); }

components.name: Accordion Toggle
components.description: Circular +/x chip used on the FAQ; the '+' rotates 135deg and fills Signal Orange when its item opens.
components.css: .ds-toggle { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 9999px; background: var(--color-primary-light); color: var(--color-primary); font-family: var(--font-heading); font-size: 22px; line-height: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 250ms ease-in-out, background 150ms ease-in-out, color 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-toggle:hover { background: var(--color-primary-muted); color: #fff; }

narrative.overview: The site looks like the surface of someone who builds, and it leaves the construction visible on purpose: hand-drawn Caveat annotations in the margins, numbered section rules, small selection handles bookending dividers, and cards that wear Figma-style selection frames. Underneath the marks, the system is disciplined and flat. Surfaces are paper-white or a cool off-white separated by hairline borders rather than shadows, type carries the hierarchy (a tight Hubot Sans over a calm Inter), and Signal Orange is the one voice that carries emphasis and state. Depth is earned, not ambient: a card lifts, a border lights, a comet traces once, only on interaction or scroll-into-view. Density is editorial, with 96px section rhythm and a 720px reading column keeping long pages calm.
keyCharacteristics: Visible construction: Caveat annotations, numbered rules, selection handles, tool-vernacular marks
Flat by default; hairline borders carry structure, shadow or motion only on state
Hubot Sans headings over Inter body, with Signal Orange as the single accent
Editorial rhythm: 96px section spacing, 720px reading column, 1186px max width
Evidence-first, calm, and honest about the making

rules.name: The Signal Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only chromatic voice on the page. It may carry both emphasis and state, but it is the sole accent: never introduce a second hue to compete with it, and never let a screen turn orange-heavy. When orange appears, it should mean something.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Rule
rules.body: Depth and grouping come from paper vs. cool-paper grounds and hairline borders, not from gray boxes or tinted panels. Reach for a background change or a hairline before a fill.

rules.name: The Annotation Rule
rules.body: Caveat is reserved exclusively for hand-drawn craft marks and never sets UI, labels, or body copy. Its rarity is what makes it read as a human mark.

rules.name: The Title Case Rule
rules.body: Headings render in Title Case as intentional house style. Keep it consistent; do not mix sentence-case headings into the same hierarchy.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow, a border-color shift, a 1px lift, or the marquee comet appears only in response to state, and then settles back. Ambient shadows and floating cards are out of language.

dos: Do set headings in Hubot Sans (Title Case, negative tracking) over Inter body, and hold reading columns near 720px.
Do keep surfaces flat and let hairline borders and paper/cool-paper grounds carry structure; reach for a shadow only as a state response.
Do treat Signal Orange as the single accent for both emphasis and state, and make each orange mean something.
Do reserve Caveat for hand-drawn craft marks and Menlo for system markers and code.
Do reuse the selection-frame vernacular (5px square handles, corner frames, the comet) when an element should read as an actionable object.
Do respect reduced-motion and keep visible keyboard focus on every interactive element.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, or let a screen become orange-heavy.
Don't add ambient shadows, floating cards, or glassmorphism.
Don't use purple-to-blue SaaS gradients, icons inside decorative circles, pill-shaped everything, or ambient animated blobs.
Don't add motion that exists only to be noticed; if it does not mark state or reveal once, cut it.
Don't replace this visual world; all work extends the existing system and connects to its tokens/components (ryan-design-taste + apply-design-system are binding).
